PRIMARY CARE NOTE   Date: 2026-07-05
56M, annual check-up.

S:
Patient presents for routine yearly visit. Feels generally well. Works full time as a rideshare and delivery driver, usually 45 to 50 hours per week across two apps. Reports long periods of sitting and irregular meals on the road. Over the past month he has noticed wheezing and chest tightness when walking quickly in cold air-conditioned buildings and after carrying heavy orders up stairs, easing within a few minutes of rest. Never smoker. Drinks 1 to 2 beers on weekends. Taking iron supplement most days.

O:
BP 124/78, HR 72, RR 14, Temp 98.0 F, SpO2 98% on room air. Weight 201 lb, BMI 29.
General: well appearing, in no distress.
HEENT: normal.
CV: regular rate and rhythm, no murmur.
Lungs: clear to auscultation bilaterally at rest.
Abdomen: soft, nontender.
Extremities: no edema.
Labs (prior week): A1c 6.1%, Hgb 12.8 g/dL, lipid panel within goal, TSH normal.

A/P:
1. Possible mild intermittent asthma; will trial albuterol. Albuterol inhaler 2 puffs before exertion or as needed for wheezing. Inhaler technique reviewed. Spirometry ordered. Advised to keep a symptom diary for the next month.
2. Prediabetes, counseled on diet and exercise. Suggested packing meals for work days, swapping soda for water, and a 15-minute walk during breaks. Repeat A1c in 6 months.
3. Anemia, stable on recheck. Continue iron supplement every other day to reduce stomach upset. Repeat CBC in 3 months.
4. Health maintenance: colorectal screening discussed; FIT kit given. Influenza vaccine offered in the fall.

Return in 6 weeks to review spirometry and symptom diary, sooner if breathing worsens.
